summary:
FireLoom is a web app for emergency responders, firefighters, land managers and scientists to explore satellite-detected active-fire hotspots across Sarawak, Malaysia. It brings together NASA FIRMS observations from MODIS, which provides the longer historical record, and VIIRS, which continues observations with greater detail. Because the instruments differ in resolution, sensitivity and observation times, their raw hotspot counts cannot be compared directly. FireLoom uses overlapping observations to adjust VIIRS counts to the MODIS Aqua reference, creating a more consistent time series.

The app’s color-coded burning calendar shows monthly hotspot activity from 2003 to the latest available observations. Users can explore seasonal patterns and long-term changes, compare activity with the historical median, view hotspot locations on a map, select a date or date range, draw a smaller area within Sarawak, and download hotspot records for their search as a CSV. A date with no accepted detections does not confirm that no fire occurred; hotspot observations are not counts of confirmed separate fires or estimates of burned area.
details:
1. The Challenge:

MODIS provides a long historical record of fire hotspots, while VIIRS continues satellite observations with greater spatial detail. Because these instruments observe fires differently, their raw hotspot counts may change when the observing sensor changes. This can make it difficult to tell whether a change in the record reflects fire activity or the change in satellite instrument.

Emergency responders, firefighters, land managers, and researchers need a clear way to explore fire activity across time, recognize seasonal patterns, and compare recent observations with historical conditions.


2. FireLoom's approach

FireLoom combines MODIS and VIIRS hotspot observations and adjusts VIIRS values to the MODIS Aqua reference scale. The resulting harmonized series is displayed through an interactive map, historical burning calendar, trend charts, and downloadable CSV files.

Users can select dates and draw an area of interest on the map or enter coordinates. The selected filters apply to the map, statistics, charts, and downloads.

3. Project Features

(a) Harmonize

Adjust MODIS and VIIRS hotspot observations to a common MODIS Aqua reference scale so activity can be compared across the satellite record.

(b) Explore

Select a date or date range and a map area to inspect harmonized hotspot activity. The map and calendar help users see where activity occurred and when.

(c) Analyze

Review daily activity, seasonal trends, historical peaks, and how selected activity compares with the historical median.

4. Targeted Users

Emergency responders, Fire fighters, Land managers, Researchers

5. Project Interface

(a) Explore Fire Activity in Sarawak

(b) Interactive Exploration & Historical Burning Calendar

Users can filter by date and focus on an area of interest using drawn shapes or entered coordinates. Users can display hotspot activity in context with mapped locations.
Users also can click on the cell in burning calendar, the hotspot will be displayed on the map.

(c) Analytical Dashboard - Trends

Seasonal charts contrast the selected year with the historical monthly median.
(c) Analytical Dashboard - Insights

Historical rankings show the most active months and years. Methodology notes explain the metrics, while CSV exports provide hotspot observations and daily or monthly summaries.

6. DEVELOPMENT, INNOVATION & IMPACT

Technology and implementation

• Satellite data: NASA FIRMS active-fire hotspot observations from MODIS and VIIRS.

• Backend: Python API using FastAPI and Uvicorn

• Frontend: React browser interface, with Node.js and npm used in the development workflow.

• Maps and analytics: Leaflet map with OpenStreetMap attribution, historical activity calendars, comparative charts, and CSV downloads.

• Deployment: Public Render-hosted web application

What makes FireLoom creative

FireLoom addresses the challenge of comparing observations from instruments that do not measure hotspots in exactly the same way. By placing the observations on a common reference scale and presenting them through a Sarawak-focused map and calendar, FireLoom helps users focus on activity patterns across time

Intended impact

FireLoom supports fire monitoring and preparedness by helping users explore where hotspot activity occurs, identify periods that have historically shown higher activity, and compare selected observations with historical patterns. This information can help users decide which places may warrant closer attention.

Factors and scientific limitations

Satellite hotspots are thermal detections. They are not confirmed counts of separate fires, estimates of burned area, or measurements of fire severity. A day with no accepted detections does not prove that no fire occurred. Harmonized values can be fractional, and comparisons for small areas may be less certain because the calibration is based on broader-area totals. The latest observations may also be provisional.
